references.text: Philip of Bethsaida is mentioned again in John 12:21, where it is confirmed that he was from Bethsaida in Galilee.
Andrew and Peter (Simon) are called as disciples in John 1:40-42, just before Philip is called. Philip was from the same town as them.
Philip appears as a central disciple in John 6:5-7, where Jesus asks him about bread for the crowd. This event takes place near Bethsaida (Luke 9:10).
In Luke 9:10, Bethsaida is mentioned as the place where Jesus withdrew with his disciples, confirming the town's significance in the gospel narrative.
In Matthew 11:21, Jesus mentions Bethsaida among the cities that had seen his miracles but did not repent.
Andrew and Peter (Simon) are also called in Mark 1:16-18, where they are described as fishermen by the Sea of Galilee. Bethsaida was located on this sea.
In John 1:45-46, Philip finds Nathanael and tells him about Jesus, which is the immediate continuation after Philip's hometown is mentioned.
